newsitem.title: UK: BADMINTON-CHINA RULES THE ROOST AS CHAMPIONS FALL.
newsitem.headline: BADMINTON-CHINA RULES THE ROOST AS CHAMPIONS FALL.

text.p: Olympic gold medallist Poul-Erik Hoyer-Larsen and world champion Heryanto Arbi were both beaten in the All England semifinals as China ruled the roost on Friday.
The two men, who have each won the All England title twice, both fell to Chinese players.

With China's world champion Ye Zhaoying and number two seed Gong Zhicao winning the women's semifinals, Saturday's singles finals -- men and women -- will both be all-Chinese affairs for the first time in the championships' history.
Denmark's Hoyer-Larsen lost to joint ninth seed Dong Jiong, the man he had beaten in Atlanta to take the Olympic title.
It was sweet revenge for the talented Chinese who won 15-8 15-10 with something to spare.
Hoyer-Larsen said: "I was making too many mistakes and my aggressive game just wasn't working. I think he learned more from his defeat against me in Atlanta than I learned from the victory."
Indonesia's Arbi also lost in straight games, 15-10 15-11, to former world junior champion Sun Jun, seeded joint three.
Arbi has slipped down the rankings following injury and has been back in full training for only three months.

On Friday Sun carried too much finesse. It was his fourth win in succession over Arbi, who may now struggle to reach a high enough international ranking to qualify to defend his world title in Scotland in May.
"I could not always read his game and it unsettled me," Arbi said. "He's got a lot of disguise."
In the women's singles, world champion Ye beat Chinese compatriot Dai Yun 11-1 5-11 11-2, while Gong swept past South Korea's Ra Kyung-min 11-3 11-2.
